claims.content: The MSIU Field Office User enters treatment claim information for the claim into the system; during claim entry, the claim form is validated manually and through the system.
The MSIU Field Office User begins entering treatment claim information for the claim into the system.
The user chooses the Form No, and the system automatically populates the Submitted Date and VSP Name fields.
The user captures the correct Voucher No, Visit Count, and Patient Type from the barcode reader based on the voucher slip stuck on the claim form.

After the correct Voucher No is entered, the system automatically populates Client Details (Address), Details of syndromes treated, Lab Test Details, Drugs Details, Success of Treatment, Referral To Treatment, and Partner Treated.
The system automatically generates the Claim number using the Hospital Code as a suffix followed by an 8-digit number.
The user selects Gender from the Male or Female options.
The user selects Doctor Name from the list populated from the VSP Staff Master.
The user selects Patient Status from the Patient Status Master.
The user does not alter the treatment information populated by the system.
The system validates every entered information during claim entry.
The system accepts the claim only when the mandatory information is complete.

The system prints a receipt document based on the information entered during claim submission, including VSP Name, Date of Submission (with date and time), number of claims mentioned, number of claims available in the header, and Treatment Form No in the detailed part.
Diverges from Step 11: The system accepts a past Date of Sale during validation; the Date of Distribution is set to the current (system) date. A future-date sale validation check is available.

claims.content: At Step 1, if the user determines during manual verification that any mandatory information is missing from the Claim (Treatment Form), the user marks the form status as 'Rejected' and sends the form back to the VSP. Exit: the form is marked Rejected and returned to the VSP.

At Step 11, if system validation finds any false data or missing mandatory information in the Claim, the claim status changes; if the status is not 'Accepted', the system stores the claim in the quarantine area and captures the reason when the status is 'Rejection' or 'Quarantine', and the field office rejects the claim back to the VSP. Quarantined forms are sent back to the VSP for verification; if the VSP returns the claim with satisfactory details, the claim is entered into the system in the following month's batch. Exit: the claim is quarantined and returned to the VSP, or, when satisfactory details are returned, it is re-entered in the following month's batch.

At Step 11, if the system captures a thumb impression that mismatches the thumb impression for the same patient (Client / Partner) on the same voucher in previous visits when such previous visits are available, the system automatically makes a count of the mismatch. If the claim from the same VSP has more than two thumb impression mismatches, the system automatically produces a warning message and inactivates the VSP. Exit: the mismatch is counted; when the more-than-two mismatch threshold is reached, the warning is produced and the VSP is inactivated.

At Step 11, if the system finds more than two fraud entries during the claim process of a particular VSP, the system automatically changes the status of that VSP to In-active. Exit: the VSP is inactivated.

claims.content: The treatment claim information has been validated successfully (mandatory information complete and no false data), validated manually and through the system, and entered into the system.

The system has accepted the claim with all mandatory master-level information (Syndrome, Clinical Examination, Diagnosis, Lab Test, Drugs, and Other Measures) entered for the treatment level based on the MSIU treatment master; Contact No is optional.

The system records and tracks the voucher number for the claim.

quality_flags.detail: [exceptionflow_exit_coverage] Exception flow claim 2 covers thumb-impression mismatch with an escalation branch when the count exceeds two, but the sub-branch where the count is two or fewer only says the mismatch is counted; it does not state whether processing continues, returns to a main flow step, or hands off/terminates. (atomic grounding: candidate remains incomplete (Explicit evidence that mismatch counts of two or fewer are recorded without warning or VSP inactivation and that claim processing continues below the threshold.; Explicit evidence for the recovery/exit behavior after a below-threshold mismatch count and after the more-than-two-mismatch threshold triggers warning and VSP inactivation.))

[exceptionflow_exit_coverage] Exception Flow claim 2 handles a thumb-impression mismatch but only defines the outcome for the >2 threshold case (warning and VSP inactivation). It does not state what happens when a mismatch occurs at or below the threshold: whether the claim continues in Main Flow, is returned, or enters another documented state. That branch therefore lacks a clear outcome. (atomic grounding: candidate remains incomplete (Explicit evidence for the <=2 mismatch branch, including whether no warning or VSP inactivation occurs and whether processing continues in the Main Flow unless another validation failure applies.; Explicit recovery/exit evidence after a mismatch is counted or after the VSP is inactivated.))

[mainflow_trigger_continuity] Main Flow step 2 restarts the use case by saying the user begins entering treatment claim information after step 1 already states that the user enters the claim information and that validation occurs during entry. This creates a duplicate start and temporal contradiction rather than a continuous flow from the trigger.

[exceptionflow_exit_coverage] Exception Flow claim 2 (Step 11 thumb-impression mismatch) describes counting mismatches and VSP inactivation when the >2 threshold is reached, but for a single/below-threshold mismatch it only says the mismatch is counted and does not state whether processing resumes at main_flow Step 11, terminates, or enters another clear state. That branch therefore lacks a clear continuation or exit outcome.

inconsistency_hints: The Trigger says entry of claim information into the system begins, but Main Flow step 1 occurs 'Before claim entry begins' and only step 2 begins entry. Thus the main flow starts before the trigger rather than continuing from it, creating a temporal contradiction/restart.

Postcondition 3 requires that the system has printed a receipt document with specified header/detail fields, but the Main Flow ends at claim acceptance and contains no step or system response that generates/prints the receipt. Therefore that postcondition is not reachable from the described flow.

Main Flow step 1 describes a manual check performed before entering claim information, while the Trigger states that entry into the system begins. This makes the first main-flow step occur before the trigger and fail to continue from it.
